references.text: Both verses use the unique combination of 'goodness and faithfulness' (hesed and emet) as a central motif for mutual loyalty and covenant relationship.
Both verses are about demanding a reliable sign or confirmation that 'goodness' (hesed) will be fulfilled in a covenant situation.
Both verses are part of the Abraham cycle and concern securing future 'goodness' (hesed) as a guarantee for the covenant relationship.
The connection lies in the contrast between human appeals for 'goodness' (hesed) and God's sovereign exercise of that same 'goodness'.
Both verses use 'faithfulness' (hesed) as a covenant guarantee in a relationship between allies, illuminating each other as examples of covenant loyalty.
Both verses use the unique combination of 'grace/goodness and faithfulness' (hesed and emet) to describe covenant-based loyalty.
Both verses ask for a visible 'sign' confirming 'goodness' (hesed), underscoring the need for evidence in covenant relationships.
